thread:
emily: Brain-dump: 'attr-federation-lite' idea to keep request docs tiny while preserving accurate billing. Short notes.

ryan: TL;DR?

emily: Keep only a compact attr fingerprint + tiny hints on hot requests. Full attribution stored separately and updated asynchronously. Avoids index blowup.

kevin: How do we compute fingerprint? deterministic + versioned?

emily: Yes. Use canonicalized tuple -> blake2b truncated 128-bit + `fp_version`. Store origin tag (proxy/sdk) + confidence.

ryan: What about partial data (edge only has tenant id)?

emily: Mark `provisional=true` and write a small local report. Reconciler later writes `attr_records` and emits correction events keyed by fingerprint.

deploy-bot: feature-flag telemetry.attr_federation_lite enabled on staging.

kevin: Need caps to avoid explosion. Propose per-tenant active-fp limit + fallback to coarse account-level fingerprint when exceeded. Alert on high churn.

emily: Good. Also add `cost_hint` (low/med/high) for realtime cost dashboards so we don't need pricing lookup on hot path.

ryan: Consumers: dashboards read provisional stream (show provisional badge), billing consumes reconciled MV. Backfills produce correction events too.

kevin: Add `origin_ts` and `attr_ttl_days` so downstream joiners can handle late arrivals. Encrypt attr_records and restrict ACLs.

emily: I'll spin a tiny RFC with schema (attr_fp, fp_version, provisional, origin, cost_hint) and a prototype script to simulate fingerprint churn. Tagging @ryan @kevin.
